chains.title: GATA2-bound LMO1 distal enhancer promotes adrenergic neuroblastoma
chains.element: dELS cCRE EH38E1518342 in LMO1 intron 1

links.claim: On the LMO1 minus strand, plus-strand ref C corresponds to G and retains a GATA motif, whereas plus-strand alt A corresponds to T and creates TATA. GATA2 is the proposed allele-specific factor: the literature supports a GATA-to-TATA switch at this SNP affecting neuroblastoma initiation, and E07 directly reports a GATA2 ChIP-seq peak containing chr11:8233861 in SK-N-SH. This supports ref-greater GATA2 binding, though allele-specific GATA2 occupancy is not itself shown. QBiC-SELEX coverage for GATA2 was not_checked because no QBiC screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup was provided.
The variant lies in distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1518342, a super-enhancer region in LMO1 intron 1 with DNase and H3K27ac signal.
The element is proposed to regulate LMO1, the nearest protein-coding gene and the strongest L2G gene at this locus; direct enhancer-promoter contact is not provided.
The relevant context is the adrenergic neuroblastoma state, supported by the GATA/TATA regulatory switch literature and by GATA2 ChIP-seq occupancy at the variant in SK-N-SH.

The ref C/GATA allele is predicted to increase GATA2-bound LMO1 enhancer activity and LMO1 expression in adrenergic neuroblastoma cells, promoting the adrenergic state and increasing neuroblastoma initiation/risk; the alt A/TATA allele is protective. The allele direction is supported by GATA-to-TATA functional literature and allelic imbalance favoring the G-containing strand, but the GATA2-specific activity and LMO1 expression change remain inferred.

predictions: Allele-specific GATA2 ChIP-qPCR or ChIP-seq shows stronger GATA2 occupancy on the ref C/G-containing allele than on the alt A/T allele at EH38E1518342 in SK-N-SH or adrenergic neuroblastoma cells.
Allele-specific reporter assays show higher enhancer activity for ref C than alt A in neuroblastoma cells, and GATA2 perturbation reduces this activity.
LMO1 expression is higher with the ref C/G allele, and CRISPR editing of rs2168101 changes LMO1 expression and adrenergic-state markers.
The EH38E1518342 element contacts the LMO1 promoter in neuroblastoma cells.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GATA2 occupancy at the rs2168101-containing element is not detected in SK-N-SH or other adrenergic neuroblastoma cells.
Reporter assays or CRISPR SNP editing show no ref-vs-alt effect on LMO1 enhancer activity or LMO1 expression in neuroblastoma cells.
The element does not contact the LMO1 promoter in neuroblastoma cells.

chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated allelic effect at rs2168101
predictions: No allele-specific transcription-factor binding at rs2168101.
No allele-specific effect of rs2168101 on LMO1 enhancer activity or LMO1 expression.
The GWAS signal is explained by linkage disequilibrium with another causal variant, by a passenger mutation, or by no functional allelic effect at this site.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GATA2 binding at the element is demonstrated.
The ref C/G allele is shown to increase LMO1 enhancer activity and LMO1 expression in neuroblastoma cells.
Functional assays show that rs2168101 itself, rather than a linked variant, changes neuroblastoma-relevant phenotypes.

chains.title: Alternative GATA3-mediated LMO1 enhancer mechanism
chains.element: dELS cCRE EH38E1518342 in LMO1 intron 1

links.claim: The ref C/G allele retains a GATA motif and the alt A/T allele creates TATA, so a GATA-family factor is predicted to bind ref more strongly. GATA3 is proposed as an alternative GATA-family factor because the motif literature does not resolve which GATA factor binds. However, the provided GATA2 ChIP-seq peak in SK-N-SH argues more directly for GATA2, and no GATA3 expression, ChIP, or perturbation evidence is provided. QBiC-SELEX coverage for GATA3 was not_checked because no QBiC screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup was provided.
The variant lies in the same distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1518342 in LMO1 intron 1.
The enhancer is proposed to regulate LMO1, the nearest gene and top L2G gene; direct contact is not shown.
The relevant context is the adrenergic neuroblastoma state, supported by the GATA/TATA switch literature, but GATA3-specific involvement is not supported.

Ref C would increase GATA3-dependent LMO1 enhancer activity and LMO1 expression in adrenergic neuroblastoma cells, promoting neuroblastoma risk; alt A would be protective. This is an alternative factor hypothesis, not a directly supported GATA3 mechanism.

predictions: GATA3 is expressed in SK-N-SH or adrenergic neuroblastoma cells and binds the ref C/G allele more strongly than the alt A/T allele.
GATA3 knockdown or inhibition reduces LMO1 enhancer activity and LMO1 expression in neuroblastoma cells.
The ref allele increases reporter activity in a GATA3-dependent manner, while GATA2 perturbation has little effect.
falsified_if: GATA2, not GATA3, is shown to be the allele-specific factor at this element.
GATA3 is not expressed in SK-N-SH or adrenergic neuroblastoma cells, or GATA3 perturbation does not alter LMO1 enhancer activity or expression.

grades_v0.reason: E06f and E06g support a GATA/TATA motif switch affecting neuroblastoma initiation, but they do not directly demonstrate GATA2 binding or allele-specific GATA2 occupancy. This is motif-level and GATA-family indirect evidence.
E01 places the variant in an LMO1 intron, and E03 directly shows it lies within dELS EH38E1518342 with DNase and H3K27ac signal.
E02 shows LMO1 as the nearest protein-coding gene and E05 gives LMO1 as the top L2G gene, but no direct enhancer-promoter contact or perturbation evidence is provided.
E06g and E06h directly support the relevance of the adrenergic neuroblastoma state and a GATA/TATA regulatory switch, though SK-N-SH itself is not specifically assayed.

The allele-direction and risk direction are broadly supported by E06f/E06g, but the claim over-claims GATA2-bound enhancer activity and LMO1 expression changes that are not directly shown in the cited evidence.
The cited evidence identifies a GATA motif affected by the SNP but does not show GATA3 binding or distinguish GATA3 from GATA2.
E01 and E03 directly place the variant in the same dELS EH38E1518342.
E02 and E05 support LMO1 as the nearest and top L2G gene, but the enhancer-gene link remains indirect without contact or perturbation evidence.
E06g and E06h support the adrenergic neuroblastoma context, but the specific GATA3 involvement is not supported.
The allele/risk direction is supported by GATA-family literature, but GATA3-dependent enhancer activity and LMO1 expression changes are not shown.
The GATA2-specific binding claim is not demonstrated; the evidence only supports a GATA-family motif effect and does not distinguish GATA2.
E03 directly shows the variant lies in EH38E1518342 and lists RIC3 among nearby genes.
The evidence does not support RIC3 as the regulated gene rather than LMO1; E05 instead ranks LMO1 far above RIC3, and no RIC3-specific expression or contact evidence is cited.
No evidence IDs are cited for the cell-type link, and the provided SK-N-SH context does not establish RIC3 as the relevant target.
E05 does not show allele-specific GATA2 binding altering RIC3 expression or a RIC3-mediated neuroblastoma phenotype.

grades_final.reason: GATA2 binding at the variant is inferred from a GATA-to-TATA motif change plus a GATA2 ChIP-seq peak in SK-N-SH, but E07 is not allele-specific and E09d assays allelic imbalance in RNA/reporter, not GATA2 occupancy. QBiC coverage is not_checked; a qbic_tf_detail lookup for GATA2 should be performed if coverage is invoked.

E03 directly places the variant in dELS EH38E1518342 with DNase/H3K27ac cCRE support, and E09c supports a super-enhancer in LMO1 intron 1. The claim is about the element, not direct enhancer-promoter contact.

E02 shows LMO1 is nearest and E05 gives strong LMO1 L2G, but the claim that the element regulates LMO1 remains a proposed regulatory link without direct contact or perturbation; L2G/proximity are indirect.

E06g directly supports the adrenergic neuroblastoma state and GATA/TATA switch, and E07 supports GATA2 occupancy in SK-N-SH. The cell-type context is supported, although allele-specific GATA2 activity is not.

Allele direction is supported by GATA-to-TATA functional literature (E06f/E06g), risk association (E09c), and allelic imbalance/reporter assays favoring the G-containing strand (E09d). However, the claim specifically requires GATA2-bound enhancer activity and LMO1 expression change in the relevant cells; GATA2-specific activity and the LMO1 expression consequence remain inferred rather than directly shown.

The only support is a GATA-family motif change at the SNP (E06f/E06g); no GATA3 ChIP, expression, allele-specific binding, or perturbation evidence is provided. GATA3 is an alternative GATA-family candidate without direct coverage. QBiC coverage is not_checked and should be checked via qbic_tf_detail if used.
E01 and E03 directly place the variant in dELS EH38E1518342; this element claim is independent of GATA3 and is supported.
E02 shows LMO1 is nearest and E05 gives top LMO1 L2G, but element-to-LMO1 regulation is proposed without direct contact or perturbation, so the gene link is indirect.
E06g/E06h support an adrenergic neuroblastoma context for the locus, but the GATA3-specific involvement asserted as part of this chain is not supported by any GATA3 evidence.

GATA-family allele direction and neuroblastoma risk direction are supported by E06f/E06g, but the phenotype claim is explicitly GATA3-dependent; no GATA3 perturbation, binding, or expression evidence supports that mechanism.

checks.why: Directly tests whether GATA2 occupies the rs2168101-containing element in the relevant neuroblastoma context; this is the most decision-relevant missing binding evidence.
Tests whether GATA3 is plausibly expressed in the SK-N-SH context; without expression support, the alternative GATA3 chain remains speculative.
Searches for allele-specific reporter, EMSA/ChIP, or perturbation evidence that distinguishes GATA2 from other GATA factors and supports the claimed phenotype direction.

matrix.test: Allele-specific luciferase reporter assay in SK-N-SH comparing ref C and alt A enhancer constructs

outcomes.outcome: Ref C/G enhancer construct gives higher reporter activity than alt A/T in SK-N-SH or adrenergic neuroblastoma cells.
Ref C/G gives higher reporter activity, but the effect is GATA3-dependent rather than GATA2-dependent.
Ref C/G and alt A/T give similar reporter activity.

matrix.test: Allele-specific GATA2 ChIP-qPCR or ChIP-seq at EH38E1518342 in SK-N-SH

outcomes.outcome: GATA2 occupies the element allele-specifically, with stronger binding to the ref C/G allele.
GATA3, not GATA2, occupies the element allele-specifically; GATA2 binding is weak or non-allelic.
No allele-specific GATA2 or GATA3 occupancy is detected at the element.

matrix.test: GATA2 and GATA3 knockdown in SK-N-SH with LMO1 expression and enhancer-activity readout

outcomes.outcome: GATA2 knockdown reduces LMO1 expression and/or enhancer activity, especially from the ref C/G allele.
GATA3 knockdown reduces LMO1 expression and/or enhancer activity, while GATA2 knockdown has little effect.
Neither GATA2 nor GATA3 knockdown changes allele-specific LMO1 expression or enhancer activity.

matrix.test: CRISPR SNP editing of rs2168101 in SK-N-SH or an adrenergic neuroblastoma model, measuring LMO1 expression and adrenergic-state markers

outcomes.outcome: CRISPR editing of rs2168101 from ref C/G to alt A/T reduces LMO1 expression and adrenergic-state markers.
CRISPR editing changes LMO1 expression in a GATA3-dependent manner, with GATA2 perturbation having little effect.
CRISPR editing of rs2168101 does not change LMO1 expression or neuroblastoma-relevant phenotypes.

matrix.test: GATA3 expression and perturbation in SK-N-SH

outcomes.outcome: GATA3 is not required for the allele-specific effect; GATA2 occupancy or perturbation explains LMO1 regulation.
GATA3 is expressed in SK-N-SH and GATA3 perturbation alters LMO1 enhancer activity or expression.
No GATA-family factor shows allele-specific functional effects at this element.

next_experiment: Allele-specific luciferase reporter assay in SK-N-SH comparing ref C and alt A enhancer constructs, with GATA2 perturbation as a secondary arm; this is the cheapest test that separates the top two chains C1 and C4 by asking whether rs2168101 itself confers allele-specific enhancer activity in the relevant cell context.
